180: Returns the human-readable Git diff of a pull request. This tool takes the repository and a pull request identifier, then retrieves the changes it proposes as a readable diff. It is typically used during review, and it returns the added and removed lines across the files the pull request touches.
181: Get the pull request information for a repository. The response contains the analysis of the pull request. This tool takes the repository and a pull request identifier, then retrieves that pull request along with Codacy's analysis of it, returning its details together with the code-quality findings for the proposed changes.
182: List pull requests from a repository that the user has access to. You can search this endpoint for either last-updated (default), impact or merged. This tool takes the repository with an optional sort or filter, then returns the accessible pull requests, each with its title, status, and related analysis summary.
183: List the patterns of a tool available for a repository in Codacy. This tool takes the repository and a tool identifier, then retrieves the analysis patterns that tool offers for the repository. It is typically used to review configuration, and it returns each pattern with its identifier and description.
184: Get analysis tools settings of a repository. This endpoint returns the analysis tools available in Codacy for a repository. This tool takes the repository identifier and retrieves its configured analysis tooling, returning each available tool together with its current settings and whether it is enabled for the repository.
185: List all code analysis tools available in Codacy. This tool takes no input and enumerates the code-analysis tools that Codacy supports. It is typically used to see what can be enabled, and it returns each tool with its name, identifier, and the languages or checks it covers.
186: List available ClickHouse databases. This tool takes no input and queries the ClickHouse server for the databases it hosts. It is typically used to explore what data exists, and it returns the names of the databases available on the connected server.
187: List available ClickHouse tables in a database, including schema, comment, row count, and column count. This tool takes a database name, then enumerates its tables. It is typically used to understand the data model, and it returns each table with its schema, comment, row count, and column count.
188: Run a SELECT query in a ClickHouse database. This tool takes a SELECT statement with the target database, then executes that read-only query against ClickHouse. It is typically used to retrieve data, and it returns the result rows produced by the query.
189: Count emails received for each day in a date range. This tool takes a start and end date, then tallies how many emails arrived on each day within that range. It is typically used to see volume over time, and it returns the per-day counts across the requested date range.
190: Get the full content of a specific email by its ID. This tool takes an email identifier, then retrieves that message in full. It is typically used after a search, and it returns the email's sender, recipients, subject, date, and complete body content.
191: Search emails within a date range and/or with specific keywords. This tool takes an optional date range together with optional keywords, then searches the mailbox for matching messages. It is typically used to find correspondence, and it returns the matching emails with their sender, subject, and date.
192: Add a business insight to the memo. This tool takes the text of an insight, then appends it to the running business-insights memo. It is typically used to record a finding during analysis, and it returns confirmation once the insight has been added to the memo.
193: Create a new table in the SQLite database. This tool takes a CREATE TABLE statement describing the table and its columns, then creates that table in the SQLite database. It is typically used to set up storage, and it returns confirmation once the table has been created.
194: Get the schema information for a specific table. This tool takes a table name, then retrieves that table's structure from the SQLite database. It is typically used before querying, and it returns the column definitions including names, types, and constraints for the requested table.
195: List all tables in the SQLite database. This tool takes no input and queries the SQLite database for the tables it contains. It is typically used to explore the schema, and it returns the names of all tables currently defined in the database.
196: Execute a SELECT query on the SQLite database. This tool takes a SELECT statement, then runs that read-only query against the SQLite database. It is typically used to retrieve records, and it returns the result rows produced by the query.
197: Execute an INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE query on the SQLite database. This tool takes a data-modifying statement, then runs it against the SQLite database to add, change, or remove records. It is typically used to update stored data, and it returns how many rows were affected by the operation.
198: Create a new branch in a GitLab project. This tool takes the project and a name for the new branch, optionally with a source branch to start from, then creates that branch. It is typically used to begin new work, and it returns the details of the branch that was created.
199: Create a new issue in a GitLab project. This tool takes the project along with a title and optional description, labels, and assignees, then opens a new issue there. It is typically used to track a task or bug, and it returns the details of the issue that was created.
200: Create a new merge request in a GitLab project. This tool takes the project, the source and target branches, and a title with optional description, then opens a merge request proposing those changes. It is typically used to request review and merging, and it returns the details of the new merge request.
201: Create or update a single file in a GitLab project. This tool takes the project, file path, content, branch, and a commit message, then writes that file, creating it or replacing its contents. It is typically used to commit one change, and it returns the resulting commit information.
202: Create a new GitLab project. This tool takes a project name along with optional settings such as visibility and description, then creates that project under your account or namespace. It is typically used to start something new, and it returns the details of the project that was created.
203: Fork a GitLab project to your account or specified namespace. This tool takes the source project and an optional target namespace, then creates a fork of it. It is typically used to build on an existing project, and it returns the details of the forked project.
204: Get the contents of a file or directory from a GitLab project. This tool takes the project and a path, optionally with a branch or ref, then retrieves the file content or directory listing at that path. It is typically used to inspect project files, and it returns the contents or listing found there.
205: Push multiple files to a GitLab project in a single commit. This tool takes the project, a target branch, a set of file paths with their contents, and a commit message, then commits all of them together. It is typically used to apply a batch of changes, and it returns the resulting commit information.
206: Search for GitLab projects. This tool takes a search query with optional filters, then finds matching projects on GitLab. It is typically used to discover repositories, and it returns each matching project with its name, namespace, description, and basic details.
207: Extracts structured data as JSON from a web page given a URL using a Natural Language description of the data. This tool takes a page URL together with a plain-language description of the fields to capture, then reads the page and returns the requested information as structured JSON.
208: 路线规划服务，计算出发地到目的地的距离、路线用时、路线方案。用户需提供出发地与目的地的位置信息，工具据此规划出行路线，并返回该路线的总距离、预计用时以及分段的路线方案等数据，便于安排从起点到终点的行程。
209: 计算多个出发地和目的地的距离和路线用时。用户需传入多个出发地与目的地的位置信息，工具会据此批量计算各出发地到各目的地之间的距离与预计路线用时，并以矩阵形式返回结果，便于在多个地点之间进行出行比较与规划。
210: 地理编码服务。用户输入一个文字地址或地点名称，工具会进行地理编码解析，将其转换为对应的经纬度坐标，并返回匹配到的结构化地址信息，便于在地图上定位该地点或用于后续的路线规划与检索。
211: 通过IP地址获取位置信息。用户需提供一个 IP 地址，工具会据此进行 IP 定位，估算该地址对应的大致地理区域，并返回所在的国家、省份、城市等行政区划信息，常用于粗略判断访问来源所处的位置。
212: 地点详情检索服务。用户需提供某个地点的标识或 POI ID，工具会据此检索该地点的详细资料，并返回其名称、地址、经纬度坐标、类别以及联系方式和营业信息等内容，便于进一步了解该地点的具体情况。
213: POI智能标注。用户传入地点相关的信息，工具会对该兴趣点进行智能识别与标注，匹配出对应的 POI，并返回其名称、类别、坐标及所属区划等标注结果，便于对地点进行规范化的识别与归类。
214: 全球逆地理编码。用户输入一组经度与纬度坐标，工具会在全球范围内进行逆地理编码，解析该坐标所对应的实际位置，并返回结构化的地址信息，包括国家、省市、区县及附近的街道或地标等描述。
215: 根据城市和道路名称查询具体道路的实时拥堵评价和拥堵路段、拥堵距离、拥堵趋势等信息。用户需提供城市与道路名称，工具据此查询该道路的实时交通状况，并返回拥堵评价、拥堵路段、拥堵距离以及拥堵趋势等数据。
216: 地点检索服务（包括城市检索、圆形区域检索、多边形区域检索）。用户可按城市、圆形区域或多边形区域提供检索条件，工具会在相应范围内检索匹配的地点，并返回每个结果的名称、地址与坐标等信息，便于查找目标区域内的地点。
217: 通过行政区划代码或者经纬度坐标获取实时天气信息和未来5天天气预报。用户需提供行政区划代码或经纬度坐标，工具据此查询该地点的天气，并返回当前的实时天气以及未来5天的预报，包括温度、天气状况与风力等信息。
218: Gets all available crypto tickers. This tool takes no input and retrieves the list of cryptocurrency tickers that the service supports. It is typically used to discover what can be queried, and it returns the available crypto ticker symbols along with their basic identifying details.
219: Get news for a company. Args: ticker: Ticker symbol of the company (e.g. AAPL, GOOGL). This tool takes a company's ticker symbol, then retrieves recent news articles about that company, returning each item with its headline, source, date, and a link so the latest coverage can be reviewed.
220: Gets historical prices for a crypto currency. This tool takes a cryptocurrency identifier with an optional date range, then retrieves its past price history. It is typically used for charting or analysis, and it returns the historical prices over time for the requested cryptocurrency.
221: Get the current / latest price of a company. Args: ticker: Ticker symbol of the company (e.g. AAPL, GOOGL). This tool takes a company's ticker symbol, then retrieves the most recent available share price for it, returning the latest price together with the symbol it corresponds to for quick reference.
